source_block.bori: BORI CE Sauptika Parva ch. 10–16 (Aishika sub-parva), Debroy translation vol. 7 (chapter-group citations): Yudhishthira's grief and Draupadi's vow; Bhima's pursuit with Nakula; Vasudeva's warning (the brahmashira, the Sudarshana episode); the Ganga bank, Vyasa and the rishis, the aishika; Arjuna's weapon; Narada and Vyasa; withdrawal and the wombs of the Pandava women; Krishna's promise and curse; the gem given up and brought to Draupadi; Yudhishthira wears it.
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, vulgate numbering = Ganguli): Sauptika Parva, Aishika Parva adhyayas 10–11 (Yudhishthira's shoka, Draupadi's prayopavesha pratijna, Bhima rides), 12–13 (Shri Krishna's warning; the pursuit; the Ganga-tata; the aishika), 14 (Arjuna's astra; Narada and Vyasa between the astras), 15 (upasamhara; the garbha), 16 (Krishna's vachana; the mani; Draupadi; Yudhishthira wears it).
source_block.divergence: Section/adhyaya numbers follow the vulgate (Ganguli = Gita Press); BORI CE chapters are cited at chapter-group level only. Omitted for length: Dhrishtadyumna's charioteer bringing the news, Yudhishthira's lament, Krishna's tale of Ashwatthama asking for the Sudarshana discus at Dvaraka, the names of Krishna's horses, Krishna's full curse (three thousand years of wandering, told only as 'walks away alone'), and the later dialogue on why Arjuna could withdraw his weapon. Nakula drove Bhima's chariot in the texts; on the ride plate Bhima holds the reins himself and Nakula is not drawn. Arjuna dismounts to loose his weapon; Krishna stands beside him on foot. Ashwatthama's kusha-grass garment is drawn as a rough grass cloak over his locked armor so the lock reads across plates. The weapon on the wombs of the Pandava women is told only as 'the unborn heir' — no woman, unborn child or baby is ever drawn; Uttara and Parikshit are not named.
source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: Draupadi's vow for the jewel, Bhima's pursuit, Krishna's warning, Krishna, Arjuna and Yudhishthira following in Krishna's chariot, Ashwatthama at Vyasa's hermitage on the Ganga, the blade of grass turned into the brahmashira, Arjuna's answering weapon with a blessing for all, Narada and Vyasa between the weapons, Arjuna's withdrawal, Ashwatthama's turning of the weapon on the Pandava unborn, Krishna's promise that the child will live, the jewel surrendered and brought to Draupadi, Yudhishthira wearing it.
